players.product: 8-inch and 12-inch wafer foundry and technology services (fabs in Shanghai, Beijing, Tianjin, Shenzhen)

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 operating detail (interim results): wafer shipments rose 14.9% to 5,379 thousand standard logic 8-inch-equivalent wafers (4,682 thousand in H1 2025); average selling price US$966 per wafer versus US$903; wafer revenue US$5,196.8 million, up 22.9%; net cash from operating activities US$3,207.1 million, up 252.7%, mainly on higher cash received from sales of goods; government funding in other operating income US$154,083 thousand. H1 revenue by region China 89.6%, America 8.7%, Eurasia 1.7%; wafer revenue by application smartphone 17.8%, computer and tablet 14.7%, consumer electronics 45.1%, connectivity and IoT 7.0%, industrial and automotive 15.4%; 12-inch wafers 77.4% of wafer revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 shipments 5,379 thousand 8-inch-eq wafers (+14.9%); ASP US$966 per wafer; wafer revenue US$5,196.8 million (+22.9%)

quarterly_data.signal: Associate gains in H1 2026 profit (interim results): share of profit of associates and a joint venture was US$198,355 thousand (a loss of US$21,083 thousand in H1 2025), including a US$218,993 thousand share of net fair-value gains of associates, primarily from net gains on certain investment portfolios of the associates, which the company marks as not sustainable; profit before tax US$1,065,417 thousand, up 109.0%.
quarterly_data.figure: US$218,993 thousand non-recurring share of associates' fair-value gains in H1 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Capital commitments and balance sheet at June 30, 2026 (interim results): contractual commitments for machinery and equipment US$5,560,616 thousand (US$10,701,400 thousand at December 31, 2025) and for building and facility construction US$419,599 thousand (US$353,747 thousand); H1 additions to property, plant and equipment US$3,524,000 thousand and depreciation US$2,285,747 thousand, most H1 capital expenditure used for capacity expansion; inventories US$4,360,884 thousand (US$3,629,802 thousand at end-2025), of which raw materials US$2,025,829 thousand; contract liabilities US$768,461 thousand (US$599,378 thousand); cash and cash equivalents US$8,216,015 thousand (US$5,872,500 thousand), the increase mainly from cash received from sales of goods.
quarterly_data.figure: equipment purchase commitments US$5,560,616 thousand vs US$10,701,400 thousand at end-2025; H1 PP&E additions US$3,524,000 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 R&D (interim results): R&D expenses US$395.6 million, up 19.6% (7.2% of revenue). Platform progress: 28nm ULL has released several foundational IPs and interface IPs, has engaged products from multiple customers across application markets and has entered mass production at a certain scale; 65nm RF-SOI - multiple products from several customers verified and in mass production; 28nm SST e-Flash - process optimisation completed with device performance the company calls industry-leading, models and PDK in progress; 90nm BCD - new low-voltage platform in product verification, medium-voltage platform has introduced multiple products for verification; 8-inch automotive electronics BCD platform entered risk production and the next-generation analog PDK was released (SOI BCD PDK under development); 0.18 micron automotive eNVM platform PDK released, eNVM IP in qualification; new large-size display driver PDK released with product design-ins ongoing. Patents granted 14,784 (12,891 invention patents) at June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 R&D US$395.6 million (+19.6%, 7.2% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: Business review and outlook (interim results): in H1 2026 demand for AI peripheral chips remained robust, overseas orders returned, localised manufacturing strengthened and the company maintained sufficient orders in hand; price increases negotiated for product categories in short supply were gradually reflected, and some customers built inventory in advance for fear of short supply and higher supply-chain prices. The company says regional conflict and geopolitical tensions drove up prices of some semiconductor raw materials, and memory capacity shifting toward AI squeezed consumer-grade memory supply, raising costs for consumer electronics, smartphones and PCs and keeping their end shipments sluggish, while automotive electronics and industrial control kept recovering. For H2 2026 it observes that upward supply-chain cost pressure has been passed through to the manufacturing segment and says it will act to mitigate the headwinds, keeping an optimistic outlook.

SMNC buyout completed (interim results): on June 12, 2026 SMIC acquired the 49% of SMNC (Semiconductor Manufacturing North China (Beijing) Corporation) held by its non-controlling shareholders - China IC Fund, Beijing Semiconductor Manufacturing and Equipment Equity Investment Center, Beijing E-town International Investment and Development, Zhongguancun Development Group and Beijing Industrial Development Investment Management - raising its ownership interest to 100%, paid in newly issued A shares; the SSE Mergers and Acquisitions Review Committee approved the deal on May 11, 2026, the CSRC approved the registration on May 21, 2026, and the new shares were registered on June 23, 2026.
